styles.name: Neubrutalism
styles.what: Thick black outlines, hard offset shadows with no blur, and two or three loud flat colours. Raw like brutalism, but tidy and friendly.
styles.origin: An evolution of web brutalism that mixes its rawness with 1990s graphic design; described by Nielsen Norman Group in 2025.
rules: Borders 2 to 4 px, solid, usually black
Shadow is one solid colour, offset about 4 px, blur 0
Two or three saturated fills on a pale ground
Headlines about twice the body size, neutral sans for body text
Padding 24 to 32 px so dense shapes can breathe
styles.motion: Fast and physical: a button moves by its shadow offset on hover and lands on press (100 to 200 ms). Marquee strips and stickers tilted a degree or two suit it. No soft fades.
a11y: Loud colour pairs still have to pass contrast: yellow with cyan does not
Condensed or decorative faces hurt paragraphs; keep body text plain
Every control needs its border, or it stops looking pressable
choose: Creator tools, indie products, developer tools, events, consumer brands that want a voice
avoid: Banking, healthcare, dense enterprise screens

styles.name: Web brutalism
styles.what: The unstyled look on purpose: default fonts, visible structure, blue links, no decoration. A statement against polish.
styles.origin: A mid-2010s reaction to the light, optimistic mainstream web, collected at brutalistwebsites.com.
rules: Browser defaults kept: serif text, underlined blue links
No rounded corners, no shadows, no gradients
Structure shown, not hidden: borders, tables, raw lists
styles.motion: None, or an instant state change. Motion would contradict the point.
a11y: It is naturally readable when the defaults are kept
Do not remove focus outlines to look raw
choose: Art, architecture and design studios, manifestos, personal sites
avoid: Anything that has to sell or convert

styles.name: Glassmorphism
styles.what: Frosted panels: a see-through fill, a blur of whatever is behind, a thin light edge and a soft shadow, floating over a colourful background.
styles.origin: Named and popularised around 2020 to 2021; assessed by Nielsen Norman Group in 2024.
rules: Fill about 15 to 40% opaque; a dark tint keeps white text readable when a bright shape drifts behind it
backdrop-filter: blur of about 10 to 25 px (NN/g shows 25 px keeping edges readable; 100 px turns the background to mush)
A 1 px light border and a soft drop shadow to lift the panel
Needs something colourful behind it, or there is nothing to frost
styles.motion: Slow drift of the shapes behind the glass, and a small lift on hover. Keep the blur radius fixed: animating blur is expensive.
a11y: Text over a see-through panel has uneven contrast: test against the lightest and darkest thing that can sit behind it
Give a solid fallback for prefers-reduced-transparency (experimental) and prefers-contrast: more
An ancestor with opacity, filter, mask or clip-path limits what the blur can see
choose: Navigation bars, overlays and cards over pictures or gradients
avoid: Long reading text, data tables, low-end devices

styles.name: Liquid Glass-inspired
styles.what: Glass that behaves like a lens: controls float in a thin clear layer above the content, pick up its colour, and have a bright rim. On the web this is an imitation, not an Apple API.
styles.origin: Apple introduced Liquid Glass in June 2025 for iOS 26 and macOS Tahoe 26. Its guidelines keep it for controls and navigation, never the content layer.
rules: Glass only on the floating layer: bars, buttons, sheets
Clearer than frosted glass: light blur, strong saturation, a bright top rim and an inner glow
Pill and capsule shapes
Over bright content, add a dark dimming layer (Apple suggests 35%)
styles.motion: Springy scale on press, and controls that merge or split. Keep it to the control layer.
a11y: Legibility was the main complaint about the real thing: check text on glass against busy content
Honour reduced transparency and increased contrast with a solid fill
Do not call a web imitation "Apple Liquid Glass"
choose: Media and photo products, Apple-platform companions, floating toolbars
avoid: Text-heavy pages, anything where the glass would sit on the content itself

styles.name: Neumorphism (soft UI)
styles.what: Shapes pushed out of, or pressed into, a surface of the same colour, drawn only with one light shadow and one dark shadow.
styles.origin: The name was coined in 2019 ("neo" plus "skeuomorphism") after a Dribbble banking concept by Alexander Plyuto; it faded by 2021 over accessibility.

tokens.fontDisplay: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", system-ui, sans-serif

rules: Element and background share one colour
Two shadows: light towards the top left, dark towards the bottom right, about 8 px offset and 16 px blur
Pressed state swaps to inset shadows
Pastel, low-contrast palette
styles.motion: A press swaps the raised shadow for an inset one in about 150 to 250 ms.
a11y: Its defining trait is low contrast: control edges fail WCAG 1.4.11 (3:1) unless you add a border or a strong icon
Raised and pressed states look alike to many people
Keep text itself at 4.5:1
choose: A few decorative controls: a music player, a smart-home dial
avoid: Forms, data-heavy apps, anything that must be scanned quickly

styles.name: Claymorphism
styles.what: Inflated, toy-like shapes: very round corners, two inner shadows that model the form, and one big soft coloured shadow underneath.
styles.origin: Named by designer Michal Malewicz in 2021 as a friendlier successor to neumorphism.

tokens.fontDisplay: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", system-ui, sans-serif
tokens.fontText: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", system-ui, sans-serif

rules: Corner radius about 30 px or more
Two inner shadows (light on top, darker below) plus one large outer shadow tinted with the shape colour
Strong, cheerful accent colours on a pale ground
styles.motion: Squash and stretch on a spring: a button flattens slightly on hover and bounces on press.
a11y: Needs strong accents and real contrast to avoid the neumorphism trap
In dark mode the fill cannot be black or the shadows vanish
choose: Children and education products, playful consumer apps, onboarding screens
avoid: Finance, legal, anything that should feel sober

styles.name: Skeuomorphism
styles.what: Controls drawn like the physical things they stand for: metal knobs, leather, paper, switches with real lighting.
styles.origin: Common in interfaces since the 1980s; Apple moved away from it with iOS 7 in 2013.

tokens.fontDisplay: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif

rules: Gradients that imitate a light from above
Bevels: a light top edge and a dark bottom edge
Material textures and real-world metaphors
Pressed states that actually move down
styles.motion: Mechanical: a key travels 2 to 3 px and returns, a switch slides, a dial turns. Short and with no bounce unless the object has one.
a11y: The metaphor gives strong affordance, which flat design lost
Texture behind text lowers contrast: check it
Ornament must not hide state
choose: Audio tools and instruments, games, products where a physical metaphor teaches the use
avoid: Content sites, large design systems that must scale

styles.name: Flat design
styles.what: No depth at all: solid fills, clear type, simple icons, strong colour. Nothing pretends to be an object.
styles.origin: Rooted in Swiss style; reached interfaces with Zune (2006), Windows Phone 7 (2010) and iOS 7 (2013).
rules: Solid colour, no gradients, no shadows
Simple geometric icons and plenty of space
Hierarchy from size, weight and colour only
styles.motion: Colour and opacity changes of 100 to 200 ms. Movement is rare and short.
a11y: With no depth cues, clickable things can look like labels: keep underlines, borders or fills on every control
A Nielsen Norman Group study is often cited for flat interfaces being slower to use for that reason
choose: Marketing sites, dashboards, documentation, anything that must load fast
avoid: Products that rely on a physical metaphor

styles.name: Material Design 3
styles.what: Google's system: tonal colour roles from one seed colour, surfaces at a few elevation levels, generous rounding and a defined motion scale.
styles.origin: Announced in 2014; Material You (Material 3) in 2021; Material 3 Expressive in 2025.
rules: Colour roles (primary, on-primary, surface, on-surface) generated from a seed colour
Corner tokens: 4, 12, 16, 28 px and full
Motion tokens: durations from 50 to 1000 ms in steps, standard easing cubic-bezier(.2, 0, 0, 1)
State layers: a tint of the content colour at 8% on hover and 12% on press
styles.motion: Use the scale: 100 to 200 ms for small changes, 300 to 500 ms for larger ones, with the standard easing. Expressive adds springs.
a11y: Colour roles are designed in contrast pairs: use on-colours with their own background
Google's own research found Expressive designs were found faster, but dropping familiar patterns hurt usability
choose: Android and Google-ecosystem products, utility apps, teams that want a ready system
avoid: Brands that must not look like an Android app

styles.name: Swiss / International Typographic Style
styles.what: A strict grid, one grotesque typeface, flush-left text and lots of white space. The layout is the decoration.
styles.origin: Switzerland, 1950s and 60s: Josef Müller-Brockmann, Armin Hofmann, Emil Ruder. Helvetica dates from 1957.
rules: A modular or 12-column grid, visibly obeyed
One sans-serif family in two or three sizes
Flush left, ragged right; asymmetric balance
Black and white plus one accent
styles.motion: Sparse and exact: text wipes along the grid, a rule that draws, one clean page-load sequence.
a11y: A naturally accessible style: high contrast, clear hierarchy
Keep line length to roughly 45 to 90 characters
choose: Editorial sites, portfolios, B2B, culture, anything led by text
avoid: Brands that want warmth or playfulness

styles.name: Minimalism
styles.what: As few elements as the job allows: one idea per screen, wide margins, one accent, and nothing ornamental.
styles.origin: From the 1960s art movement; "less is more" (Mies van der Rohe) and "less but better" (Dieter Rams).
rules: One accent colour or none
Large margins; white space does the grouping
One or two type sizes above body
Remove an element before adding one
styles.motion: Almost none: opacity and position changes of 150 to 300 ms that explain a change of state.
a11y: Do not remove affordances along with decoration: links and fields still need to look like links and fields
Thin grey text on white fails contrast quickly
choose: Premium products, portfolios, focused tools, any brief that says calm
avoid: Products that must show a lot at once

styles.name: Maximalism
styles.what: More is more: clashing colour, layered pattern, several typefaces, everything large and overlapping, held together by repetition.
styles.origin: A long-standing reaction to minimalism across art, music and interiors; on the web it shows up as dense, collaged pages.
rules: Several saturated colours at once, plus pattern
Mixed typefaces and sizes on purpose
Overlap, rotation and collage
One repeated device (a border, a colour) to keep it from falling apart
styles.motion: Busy but ordered: things tilt, bounce and trade places; marquees run. Pick one thing to move most.
a11y: Text needs its own solid backing when the page behind is patterned
Order in the markup still has to make sense to a screen reader
Loops need a pause control or reduced-motion handling
choose: Fashion, music, festivals, youth brands, campaigns
avoid: Tools, checkouts, anything people use while stressed
styles.note: Documented as an aesthetic in art and design; no single source defines it for the web.

styles.name: Bento grid
styles.what: A grid of rounded tiles of different sizes, like a lunch box. Each tile holds one feature, and bigger tiles matter more.
styles.origin: Named after the Japanese lunch box; popular since Apple product pages around 2023, with Windows Metro tiles as an earlier relative.
rules: CSS Grid with tiles spanning different numbers of columns and rows
One consistent gap and one corner radius
One idea per tile; size shows importance
Collapses to a single column on phones
styles.motion: Tiles scale a little on hover or play one small loop each. Stagger their entrance once, at most.
a11y: Visual order and DOM order drift apart easily: check the reading and tab order
Do not hide the main message in a small tile
choose: Feature overviews, product pages, dashboards, portfolios
avoid: Arguments that have to be read in order

styles.name: Editorial / magazine
styles.what: A printed page on screen: a serif headline, a standfirst, columns, pull quotes, captions and rules. Typography carries the page.
styles.origin: Carried over from print magazines and newspapers; on the web it sits close to Swiss style.

tokens.fontText: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif

rules: A display serif for headlines with a readable text serif or sans
Columns, rules, drop caps, pull quotes and captions
A clear type scale with big jumps
Images cropped with intent, text allowed to overlap them
styles.motion: Quiet: a headline that sets line by line, images that reveal with a mask, captions that fade. Scroll-driven chapters suit long pieces.
a11y: Keep measure near 45 to 90 characters and line height near 1.5
High-contrast display serifs get too thin at small sizes
choose: Publications, long-form stories, luxury and culture brands, case studies
avoid: Dense apps and tools
styles.note: A print tradition; no single source defines it as a web style.

styles.name: Y2K
styles.what: The late-1990s vision of the future: chrome, bubbly rounded type, translucent plastic, lime and hot pink, shiny gradients.
styles.origin: The look of roughly 1997 to 2004, revived in the 2020s.

tokens.fontDisplay: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", system-ui, sans-serif
tokens.fontText: ui-rounded, "SF Pro Rounded", "Arial Rounded MT Bold", system-ui, sans-serif

rules: Lime, orange and hot pink with white and chrome
Chunky rounded lettering, often outlined
Glossy gradients with a hard white highlight
Translucent plastic and bubbles
styles.motion: Bouncy and toy-like: buttons click down, stars spin, things wobble on hover.
a11y: Gradient-filled text needs a readable fallback colour and enough contrast at its lightest point
Sparkle and spin loops need reduced-motion handling
choose: Fashion, music, youth brands, nostalgia campaigns
avoid: Serious or long-lived product interfaces

styles.name: Frutiger Aero
styles.what: Glossy optimism from the Windows Vista era: sky blues and grass greens, water drops, bokeh, glassy rounded buttons.
styles.origin: Roughly 2004 to 2013. Named in 2018 after the Frutiger typeface and Windows Aero.

tokens.fontDisplay: "Frutiger", "Segoe UI", "Myriad Pro", system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, sans-serif

rules: Bright blue, green and white
Gloss: a hard highlight across the top half of buttons
Nature imagery, water and bokeh circles
Translucent rounded panels
styles.motion: Smooth and glossy: gentle glows, bubbles rising, soft fades of 200 to 400 ms.
a11y: Text over sky gradients and bokeh needs a panel behind it
Gloss highlights can cut contrast across button labels
choose: Nostalgia projects, climate and wellness brands that want an optimistic tone
avoid: Anything that must look current and neutral

styles.name: Vaporwave
styles.what: An ironic remix of 1990s computing and mall culture: pastel pink and cyan, marble busts, old window chrome, wide-spaced text.
styles.origin: Grew out of an internet music scene in 2011 and 2012.
rules: Pastel pink, lilac and cyan gradients
Serif or system type with wide letter-spacing, often uppercase
Old operating-system window frames, grids, statues, palm trees
A little VHS damage
styles.motion: Slow and dreamy: drifting gradients, a hue shift on hover, a scan line that passes now and then.
a11y: Pastel on pastel fails contrast: keep text dark
Wide-spaced uppercase text is tiring in paragraphs; use it for labels only
choose: Music, art and culture projects, merch, ironic campaigns
avoid: Mainstream commerce and tools

styles.name: Synthwave / retrowave
styles.what: A neon 1980s: a magenta sun, a perspective grid running to the horizon, chrome type, purple night sky.
styles.origin: A music and visual genre from the mid-2000s built on 1980s film and game imagery; also called retrowave or outrun.
rules: Magenta, cyan and orange on deep purple
A grid floor in perspective and a striped sun
Chrome or gradient display type, italic and uppercase
Glow on everything that is lit
styles.motion: The grid scrolls towards the viewer, glows pulse slowly, titles slide in with a streak.
a11y: Glow does not add contrast: the text colour itself has to pass
A moving grid is a vestibular trigger: stop it for reduced motion
Thin neon text is hard to read
choose: Games, music, events, retro-tech products
avoid: Calm or corporate brands

styles.name: Memphis
styles.what: Squiggles, triangles, dots and terrazzo in clashing primaries and pastels, scattered at angles. Loud, geometric and cheerful.
styles.origin: The Memphis Group, an Italian design collective led by Ettore Sottsass, 1980 to 1987.
rules: Primary colours with pink, mint and yellow, plus black outlines
Loose geometric shapes: circles, triangles, squiggles
Patterns: dots, stripes, terrazzo
Asymmetry and tilt
styles.motion: Shapes drift, rotate and bounce at different speeds; hover gives a quick tilt.
a11y: Keep patterns away from text or put a solid panel behind it
Decorative shapes should be hidden from assistive technology
choose: Events, education, playful consumer brands, posters
avoid: Sober or premium products

styles.name: Corporate Memphis
styles.what: The flat tech-company illustration style: friendly figures with long limbs and small heads in bright, flat colours.
styles.origin: Named by Mike Merrill; the best-known version, Alegria, was made for Facebook by the agency Buck in 2017.
rules: Flat bright fills, no outlines
Blobs and simple figures as decoration
Rounded cards with soft shadows
A friendly geometric sans
styles.motion: Gentle floating of illustrations, soft slide-ups of 300 to 400 ms.
a11y: Illustrations of people need alt text that says what they show, or should be marked decorative
By 2023 the style was widely seen as generic: use it knowingly
choose: Internal tools, onboarding, explainers where friendliness matters more than distinction
avoid: Brands that need to stand apart

styles.name: Art Deco
styles.what: Symmetry, stepped forms, sunbursts and fine gold lines on black or navy, with tall elegant capitals.
styles.origin: France, 1910s; named after the 1925 Paris exhibition of decorative arts.

tokens.fontText: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif

rules: Black or navy with gold, sometimes emerald or burgundy
Strict symmetry and centred layouts
Stepped shapes, chevrons, fans and sunbursts
Tall, widely spaced capitals
styles.motion: Stately: lines that draw outward from the centre, fans that open, slow fades of 400 to 600 ms.
a11y: Gold on black passes easily, gold on white does not
Wide-spaced capitals are for headings only
choose: Hotels, bars, jewellery, events, heritage brands
avoid: Casual, technical or youthful products

styles.name: Cyberpunk / neon
styles.what: A dark city at night: black panels, acid yellow and cyan neon, clipped corners, warning labels and terminal type.
styles.origin: From 1980s science fiction; Blade Runner (1982) set the visual template.

tokens.fontDisplay: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
tokens.fontText: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

rules: Near-black background with one or two neon colours
Cut corners, thin lines, hazard stripes, small technical labels
Monospace or condensed type
Glow made from stacked shadows
styles.motion: Sharp and electric: flicker on entry (once), scan lines, quick clipped wipes of 100 to 200 ms.
a11y: Flashing must stay under three times a second (WCAG 2.3.1) and loops need a stop
Glow is not contrast; thin neon text fails
Default dark is a choice: say why in the brief
choose: Games, security and developer tools, music, hardware
avoid: General audiences reading at length

styles.name: Glitch
styles.what: Deliberate digital damage: colour channels that split apart, slices that jump sideways, torn scan lines.
styles.origin: From glitch art and 1990s net.art, where broken data became the image.

tokens.fontText: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

rules: Red and cyan copies of the text offset by a pixel or two
Horizontal slices displaced with clip-path
Stepped timing, not smooth easing
Used on one element, not the whole page
styles.motion: Short bursts of 200 to 400 ms with stepped easing, then stillness. Triggered by hover, entry or an error state.
a11y: Keep bursts rare and under three flashes a second (WCAG 2.3.1)
Never glitch body text or controls people are trying to use
Turn it off for reduced motion
choose: Music, games, art, error pages, launch teasers
avoid: Reading-heavy pages, anxious contexts such as payments

styles.name: Aurora / mesh gradient
styles.what: Large, soft, blurred fields of colour that blend into each other like northern lights, usually behind plain text.
styles.origin: A descriptive label from the 2020s, not a movement. CSS has no true mesh gradient, so it is built from blurred blobs.
rules: Two to four large radial gradients, heavily blurred
A dark or very pale base so the colours glow
Plain type and few elements on top
A little grain on top hides banding
styles.motion: Very slow drift: 15 to 30 seconds per cycle, transform only. It should be barely noticeable.
a11y: Contrast changes as the colours move: test text against the brightest blob
Stop the drift for reduced motion
Animate transform, never the blur radius or gradient stops, on large areas
choose: AI and developer products, landing page heroes, anything abstract with no photo to show
avoid: Pages where a product picture would say more
styles.note: A trend label, not a documented movement.

styles.name: Grain / noise texture
styles.what: A fine speckle over flat colour or gradients, like film grain or cheap print. It removes the plastic look and hides banding.
styles.origin: A print and film artefact, reproduced on the web with an SVG noise filter.

tokens.fontDisplay: "Iowan Old Style", "Palatino Linotype", Palatino, Georgia, serif

rules: SVG feTurbulence, type fractalNoise, baseFrequency about 0.7 to 1
Overlay at low opacity with multiply or overlay blending
A small repeating tile (stitchTiles) and never a live full-screen filter
Works best over gradients and muted, printed-looking palettes
styles.motion: The grain itself stays still. If it must flicker, step it at a few frames a second on a small layer.
a11y: Grain lowers text contrast slightly: keep it behind text or very faint
Animated noise is tiring and costly: default to still
choose: Craft, food, fashion, editorial, any brand that wants a printed or analogue feel
avoid: Crisp, clinical product interfaces

styles.name: Duotone
styles.what: Every picture mapped to just two colours, a dark and a light, so mixed photography looks like one set.
styles.origin: A printing technique: a halftone made with two inks.
rules: Convert the image to greyscale first
Map shadows to one colour and highlights to another (multiply for the dark, lighten or screen for the light, or an SVG feComponentTransfer)
Use the same pair across the whole site
Pick a pair with strong lightness contrast
styles.motion: Cross-fade between two colour pairs on hover or scroll; otherwise still.
a11y: Text over a duotone photo needs a scrim or a solid panel
Check the pair itself for colour-blind confusion: lightness contrast matters more than hue
choose: Sites with mixed or weak photography, music and events, campaigns with one strong brand colour
avoid: Products where true colour matters, such as food or fashion detail

styles.name: Dark-mode-first
styles.what: The dark theme is the designed default: near-black surfaces in a few elevation steps, soft white text, one bright accent.
styles.origin: A practice, not a movement. Research from Nielsen Norman Group says light mode reads better for most people, so a dark default needs a reason.
rules: Background near black, not pure black; text off-white, not pure white
Depth from lighter surfaces, not from shadows
Accent colours less saturated than on white
Ship a light theme too, switched by prefers-color-scheme
styles.motion: The same as the light theme. Glows and gradients read stronger on dark, so use less.
a11y: Light mode performs better for most people in most conditions: offer both and respect the system setting
Pure white text on pure black causes halation for some readers
Borders need 3:1 against the surface to be seen
choose: Developer tools, media and video, games, dashboards used in dim rooms
avoid: Long-form reading for a general audience, unless a light theme is one click away

styles.name: Isometric
styles.what: Objects drawn as if seen from above at an angle with no perspective, so parallel lines never meet. Reads as a tidy little model world.
styles.origin: A technical drawing projection; familiar from games, which usually use a 2:1 pixel ratio.
rules: Three visible faces per object: top lightest, one side mid, one side darkest
True isometric uses 30° to the horizontal; pixel-friendly art uses a 2:1 slope
One light direction for every object
Flat colours; depth comes from the three tones
styles.motion: Parts lift, stack and slide along the three axes. Layers separating vertically explain how a product is built.
a11y: Isometric scenes are illustrations: describe what they show in text
Small isometric labels get hard to read at an angle; keep text flat
choose: Explaining systems, infrastructure, logistics, fintech flows, feature diagrams
avoid: Emotional or lifestyle brands

styles.name: Kinetic typography
styles.what: The words are the animation: letters, words and lines move, stretch and take turns, so reading and watching become one thing.
rules: Split text into lines, words or characters and stagger them
One typeface, very large
Movement follows the reading order
Keep the real sentence available to screen readers
styles.motion: A set headline on load (0.6 to 1.2 s), then words that react to scroll. Stagger 30 to 60 ms per word.
a11y: Split text must stay one sentence for assistive technology
Text that never stops moving needs a pause, or must end within 5 seconds (WCAG 2.2.2)
choose: SaaS and product launches with a strong line and no picture, agencies, manifestos
avoid: Pages where the message is in a picture or a demo

styles.name: Scroll-driven storytelling
styles.what: The page is a sequence: sections pin, pictures scrub and charts redraw as the reader scrolls, so the scroll bar becomes the timeline.
rules: Pin a scene and drive it with scroll progress
One change per step
Text beside the picture, never hidden behind the effect
Everything still readable as a plain page
styles.motion: Scrubbed, not timed: the reader sets the speed. Smooth scroll is optional and must not fight the trackpad.
a11y: Parallax and zooms can cause nausea: reduce to cuts for reduced motion
Pinned sections must not trap keyboard users
A 2013 Purdue study found parallax did not improve the experience by itself
choose: Brand stories, product explainers, journalism, annual reports, data stories
avoid: Task pages people visit to get something done

styles.name: 3D / immersive WebGL
styles.what: A real-time 3D scene is the page: a product you can turn, a world the camera moves through, particles that form a shape.
rules: One hero object, well lit, beats a busy scene
Camera moves tied to scroll or pointer
A still picture for no-WebGL and for reduced motion
Pixel ratio capped at 2 and the loop paused off screen
styles.motion: Slow, weighty camera moves with damping. Idle motion of a few degrees keeps the scene alive.
a11y: The canvas is invisible to assistive technology: the same content must exist as text
Large rotations and zooms should become cuts for reduced motion
Give controls a keyboard path (a slider, buttons)
choose: Product launches, hardware, automotive, games, portfolios of 3D work
avoid: Content pages, slow devices, anything that must load in a second

styles.name: Micro-interactions
styles.what: Small animated answers to what a person just did: a toggle that slides, a row that makes room, a number that settles.
rules: Each one has a trigger and feedback
Feedback within about 100 ms; most transitions 200 to 300 ms
Entering slightly slower than leaving
Springs for things people drag, so they can be interrupted
styles.motion: Only in response to input. If nothing was pressed, nothing moves.
a11y: State must also be shown without motion (text, icon, colour)
Drag needs a keyboard alternative
Announce results to screen readers with a live region
choose: Apps, dashboards, forms, checkouts, any interface used every day
avoid: Nothing: every interface benefits, in moderation

techniques.name: Organic / blob shapes
techniques.what: Soft, irregular shapes made with an eight-value border-radius, an SVG path or clip-path. A tool used inside other styles (claymorphism, Corporate Memphis), not a documented style of its own.

techniques.name: Monochrome
techniques.what: One hue in several tints and shades. A palette decision used inside Swiss, minimal or dark-first work, not a style of its own.

notReal.name: Spectromorphism
notReal.verdict: Not a design style. No design source uses it; the nearest real word, spectromorphology, is a term from electroacoustic music. If a brief asks for it, ask whether neumorphism, skeuomorphism or glassmorphism was meant.
